claim_assessments.reason: The original general isolated normal analytic germ implication is supported by the checked completion, exact model, finite tangent descent and one-open argument. The initial assertion alone supplied neither source checks nor independent acceptance.
Same mathematical statement; Algebraization_inputs bundled several distinct foundational steps and was not a stand-alone proof. Those steps are now individually assessed.

The explicit AG decomposition establishes the finite-type normal C-domain, dimension, unchanged marked completion, free full algebraic derivations and smooth complement. Retiring the omnibus assumption does not eliminate the external theorems. Application to the surface still uses the upstream analytic input.

The original statement is valid for a normal complex analytic germ smooth off the point. The conormal-dual Jacobian cokernel, not the conormal module itself, has finite support. Its finite length requires the analytic local zero-set theorem in addition to coherence.
Adds exact completion of finite modules, Tag 00MA. This justifies completing the full presentation and finite kernels but alone does not establish excellence or normal completion.
Adds faithfully flat completion, Tag 00MC. The unchanged statement is supported using the complete checked input package, not this single added citation alone.
Adds preservation of Krull dimension, Tag 07NV; it applies to the actual Noetherian analytic local ring without algebraicity.
Adds equivalence of regularity with completion, Tag 07NY. The analytic/full continuous tangent distinction remains as in the original statement.

Adds Tag 0C23, whose hypothesis is a normal local ring with normal formal fibres. The later explicit analytic excellence input supplies that hypothesis; normality alone would not have justified the inference.

Adds Cutkosky arXiv:1206.4255v3 Proposition 2.1(1). The actual read proposition says every complex analytic local ring is Noetherian, Henselian and excellent, providing normal formal fibres without assuming algebraicity.

Adds the historically reviewed analytic coherence input. Full finite presentations complete exactly; isolated support and the analytic local zero-set theorem give finite length; the full holomorphic tangent module completes to the finite continuous Jacobian kernel R^d. The zero-set consequence is explicitly listed below rather than hidden in coherence.
The exact solution and one-stage conclusion are supported after checking the precise Artin theorem and filtered-colimit equality argument. The initial assertion did not itself supply those checks.

Adds Artin Theorem 1.10: field base C, henselization of the finite-type polynomial algebra at the origin, proper maximal ideal, finite system GB=0 and formal solution (f,D). The solution in the henselization is exact.
Adds Tag 04GN. Representing entries is followed by passing to one common later pointed stage where all finitely many zero-product identities hold; stage injectivity is not assumed.
Adds Tag 06LJ. The Noetherian henselization has the same completion as the local polynomial ring; it is not itself identified with that completion.
Adds Tag 00U9. The invertible auxiliary Jacobian supports unique nilpotent lifts and the finite ambient differential basis.
Adds Tag 00U2. A finite list of denominators and identity numerators is handled on a single affine etale neighborhood of the retained point.

Adds Tag 00U4 and completes the pointed maximal-ideal/residue-field check. The compatible ambient completion is P, the exact quotient completion is P/(g), and determinacy identifies it with the original R.

The original statement correctly uses ordinary algebraic differentials of the essentially finite-type ring T and their finite Jacobian presentation, not the ordinary Kahler module of the formal power-series ring.
Adds Tag 00MC. Lifting a residue basis, Nakayama, a completed square-matrix isomorphism and faithful-flat kernel detection descend freeness of the finite module, not an arbitrary chosen formal basis.

Adds Tag 00U9. The formal chain rule includes Q_ki=sum_l Phi(g_l)*partial_k U_li, which vanishes only modulo the equation ideal. Invertible coordinate and generator matrices transport the continuous kernels; finite flat base change then proves Der_C(T)=T^d.

The original one-principal-neighborhood statement is supported by extending the full basis and successively killing finite modules and unwanted closed components away from the point. Products of denominators make the final open principal.
Adds Tag 00MC. Faithful-flat contraction descends local normality and Fitting containment, but a separate finite-normalization argument is required for the global normal open.
Adds Tag 07QW. After removing nilpotents and other components the retained finite-type C-domain is excellent.
Adds Tag 07QV. The finite normalization quotient vanishes at the normal local ring T and can be killed by localization; T is not replaced by a different normalization.
Adds Tag 00OS. The retained point is maximal with residue C, so the dimension of the finite-type domain equals dim(T)=d.
Adds Tag 00OT. Topological dimension at every point of the integral d-dimensional neighborhood is d; it is not confused with the local ring's dimension at a nonclosed point.

Adds exact Tag 00TT. Fitt_d(Omega) describes the nonsmooth locus on the pure d-dimensional neighborhood. Its local maximal-ideal-power containment rules out any positive-dimensional nonsmooth component through the point. Removing other components and multiplying all denominators retains a single affine open with the full basis and all marked invariants.

The 'unexamined' list was an audit placeholder, not a proof. Original Artin 1.10, Hironaka 3.3, Artin 3.8-3.9, Cutkosky v3 2.1(1) and the precise used Stacks passages were read. 07QY/07QZ merely corroborate; 0A1W is unnecessary. No journal-version verification or native algebraization approval is inferred.

external_assumptions.statement: For every complex analytic space X and p in X, O_X,p is a Noetherian, Henselian, excellent local ring.
external_assumptions.locator: Cutkosky, Etoiles and Valuations, 2 December 2016, Proposition 2.1(1), numbered/PDF page 4
external_assumptions.read_assessment: The actual extracted proposition and the excellence excerpt were read. It applies before algebraization and does not assume reducedness or isolatedness. The manuscript's 2017 journal version/pagination was not inspected; attribution is to this exact v3 proposition.

external_assumptions.statement: Analytic structure sheaves are coherent; kernels, cokernels, images, tensor products and Hom of coherent analytic sheaves are coherent. The nilradical has a uniform nilpotence exponent on relatively compact subsets, including for nonreduced complex spaces.
external_assumptions.locator: Grauert 1960, section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, page 15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), page 16
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Primary extracted pages read; this is also a version-matched historical analytic input. Coherence provides finite conormal-dual kernels and cokernels. Uniform nilpotence is not silently substituted for the separate isolated-zero-set argument.

external_assumptions.statement: For a proper ideal a of a complex analytic local ring (S,m), if its analytic zero-set germ is only the marked point, then radical(a)=m. Since S is Noetherian, some m^b is contained in a. In particular a finite coherent module supported at that point has finite length by applying this to its annihilator.
external_assumptions.source_version: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, version Thursday June 21, 2012
external_assumptions.locator: Version June 21, 2012, Chapter II, section 4, (4.22) Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, printed p.97
external_assumptions.read_assessment: The parent obtained the author's primary PDF at the current institutional hostname and read the exact ideal/radical statement and proof, including its complex-germ hypothesis. Passing to an analytic quotient gives the stated radical equality; finite generation gives a maximal-ideal power. The historical Grauert invocation alone was not a complete theorem statement.
external_assumptions.historical_source_limit: The old-hostname HTTPS request failed certificate hostname verification. TLS was not weakened; the author's current institutional hostname succeeded. Other historically unavailable Demailly locators were not thereby all inspected.

external_assumptions.statement: If I is an ideal of a Noetherian ring R, I-adic completion preserves injections and short exact sequences of finite R-modules, and Mhat=M tensor_R Rhat for each finite module M.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. All completed presentations, kernels, images and cokernels here are finite over Noetherian rings.

external_assumptions.statement: If I lies in the Jacobson radical of a Noetherian ring R, R to its I-adic completion is faithfully flat. In particular this holds for maximal-ideal completion of every Noetherian local ring.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to S and T; justifies finite-kernel base change, vanishing detection and ideal contraction.

external_assumptions.statement: A Noetherian local ring and its maximal-ideal completion have equal Krull dimensions.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to both the analytic input ring and the constructed algebraic local ring.

external_assumptions.statement: A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if its maximal-ideal completion is regular.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Completion preserves both dimension and embedding dimension, so a singular marked analytic point remains nonregular algebraically.

external_assumptions.statement: If (R,m) is a normal Noetherian local ring whose formal fibres are normal, then Rhat is normal; excellence or quasi-excellence is a sufficient formal-fibre hypothesis.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. The analytic normality is a hypothesis; Cutkosky v3 supplies excellence. Normality alone is not used to infer normal completion.

external_assumptions.statement: Let R be a field or an excellent discrete valuation ring, A the henselization of a finite-type R-algebra at a prime ideal, and m a proper ideal of A. Given a finite polynomial system over A, a solution in its m-adic completion and an integer c, there exists an exact solution in A agreeing with that formal solution modulo m^c.
external_assumptions.locator: Artin 1969, Theorem 1.10, printed page 26, PDF page 5; primary extraction lines 160-175
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Actual extracted original statement compared with restored transcription. Use R=C, A=(C[x]_(x))^h, m=(x)A, unknown entries (G,B), polynomial system GB=0 and formal solution (f,D). This is the original exact-solution theorem, not an approximate-zero claim or a substituted theorem.

external_assumptions.statement: The henselization of a local ring (R,m,kappa) is the filtered colimit of pointed etale R-algebras (S,q) with q over m and kappa(q)=kappa; its maximal ideal is mR^h and its residue field is kappa. Two represented elements are equal precisely when their images agree at a common later pointed stage.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.155.1 and the explicit construction and equality criterion in its proof
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement, current primary statement in raw HTML, and filtered-category proof read. Finite entries and all finite zero-product identities descend together; injectivity of a stage is not assumed.

external_assumptions.statement: For a local ring R, Noetherianity is equivalent for R and R^h (also R^sh). In the Noetherian case Rhat to (R^h)hat is an isomorphism of complete local rings.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to Q0=C[x]_(x) and H=Q0^h; H itself is not identified with P.

external_assumptions.statement: Every etale ring map R to S admits a presentation S=R[z_1,...,z_n]/(h_1,...,h_n) in which det(partial h_j/partial z_i) is invertible in S.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Invertible auxiliary Jacobian gives the differential basis and the nilpotent lifting argument for the pointed completion.

external_assumptions.statement: Etale maps are stable under localization, composition and base change. Etale algebras descend over filtered colimits; in particular an etale algebra over a localization S^(-1)A is the localization of an etale A-algebra.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived parts and current primary tag read. Finite presentation and finitely many point-preserving denominators spread the stage and its entries/identities to one finite-type affine etale C[x]-algebra.

external_assumptions.statement: If R to S is etale at a prime q over p, then pS_q=qS_q is the maximal ideal of S_q, and kappa(q)/kappa(p) is finite separable.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. The chosen pointed stage has equal residue field C, so together with nilpotent unique lifting its local completion is the chosen P.

external_assumptions.statement: Fields and finite-type ring extensions of fields are excellent.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to the retained finite-type C-domain after removing nilpotents and unwanted components.

external_assumptions.statement: A quasi-excellent ring is Nagata. In particular a quasi-excellent domain is N-1 and has finite normalization in its fraction field.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.53.5 and its proof's N-1 conclusion
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag/proof read. The finite normalization quotient vanishes after localization at the already normal T; killing that quotient yields a normal open without changing T.

external_assumptions.statement: For a finite-type integral-domain algebra S over a field, dim(S)=dim(S_m) for every maximal ideal m.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. The marked point is closed with residue C; the retained domain therefore has global dimension dim(T)=d.

external_assumptions.statement: For X=Spec(S), S a finite-type algebra over a field, topological dim_x(X) equals the maximum dimension of the irreducible components passing through x.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. Topological dimension is d everywhere on the retained integral neighborhood; local-ring dimension at a nonclosed point is not substituted.

external_assumptions.statement: For a finite-type k-algebra S, k a field, and a prime q corresponding to x in X=Spec(S), smoothness at q is equivalent to dim_kappa(q)(Omega_(S/k) tensor kappa(q))<=dim_x(X), equivalently equality. In that case S_q is regular.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived statement and current primary tag read. On the integral d-dimensional neighborhood, the minimal-generator minor criterion identifies V(Fitt_d(Omega)) with the nonsmooth locus.

external_assumptions.statement: For a Noetherian ring R, ideal a and finite submodule N of M, some c>0 satisfies a^r M intersect N = a^(r-c)(a^c M intersect N) for all r>=c.
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Archived and current primary statements read. The companion fixed-relation-determinacy report checks all three separate filtration losses and all order ranges; this is an external premise of that dependency, not a consequence of finite arithmetic.

external_assumptions.statement: Let k be Noetherian, R the H1-adic completion of a localization R1 of k[x], H=H1R with H1 proper, J an ideal of R, X=Spec(R/J), and Y=Spec(R/(J+H)). Assume X-Y is formally k-smooth as in (3.1), and fix an exact original finite free presentation L2 --g--> L1 --f--> R --> R/J --> 0. There are fixed nonnegative s,t,r such that every j>=t and pair f',g' with f'g'=0, g'=g modulo H^s and f'=f modulo H^j yield equivalent quotients by a k-automorphism of R congruent to the identity modulo H^(j-r). Exactness at L1 is not required for the approximating pair.
external_assumptions.locator: Hironaka 1969, section 3, Example I and Theorem 3.3, original 210-211, re-typeset 220-221, PDF 229-230
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Primary section and historical excerpt read. Historical attribution assessed in full in the companion unit; its geometric hypotheses are not silently replaced by the abstract finite-length hypothesis.
external_assumptions.use: Historical method attribution, not a substitute for the checked proof.

external_assumptions.statement: Artin 3.8: a quotient of k[[X]], k a field, formally smooth over k away from its closed point is isomorphic to the completed local ring of an algebraic k-scheme. Artin 3.9: if k is a field, A is the henselization of k[X] at a prime and a is a proper ideal, a quotient of its a-adic completion formally smooth over k outside V(a) is the a-adic completion of a quotient of A. The proof approximates two presentation maps with exact zero composite.
external_assumptions.locator: Artin 1969, Theorems 3.8-3.9 and proof, printed pages 32-34, PDF pages 11-13
external_assumptions.read_assessment: Actual primary extracted theorems and proof read against the historical excerpt. They establish the prior method, not tangent descent, a novelty judgment or current acceptance.
